Detailed Description

Descriptive statistics, 20+ probability distributions, hypothesis testing (t-test, ANOVA), regression models, PCA, and clustering.

◆ adtest()

std::tuple< Value, Value, Value, Value > nk::stats::adtest ( const Value & x,
double alpha = 0.05,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Anderson-Darling test for normality ([h, p, adstat, cv] = adtest(x, alpha)).

H0: x is drawn from a normal distribution with parameters estimated from the sample (mu = mean(x), sigma = std(x)).

Algorithm: sort and z-standardise, compute A² = -n - (1/n) · Σ (2i-1) · [ln Φ(z_i) + ln(1 - Φ(z_{n+1-i}))], then the Stephens-1986 small-sample adjustment A²* = A² · (1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n²). p-value from D'Agostino-Stephens (1986) piecewise rational fit for the parameters-estimated case.

Parameters
xSample data (length ≥ 8 for reliable p-values).
alphaSignificance level (default 0.05).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(h, p, adstat, cv) — decision, p-value, A²*, 5% critical value (0.752 for estimated parameters).

◆ ansaribradley()

std::tuple< Value, Value, Value, Value > nk::stats::ansaribradley ( const Value & x,
const Value & y,
double alpha,
TestTail tail,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Ansari-Bradley two-sample scale (dispersion) test ([h, p, W, Wstar] = ansaribradley(x, y, alpha, tail)).

Non-parametric H0: x and y have the same dispersion (variances are equal). The Ansari-Bradley statistic W is the sum, in the pooled sorted sample, of the V-shaped ranks 1, 2, …, ⌈N/2⌉, …, 2, 1 over positions occupied by x.

Under H0, W is asymptotically normal with closed-form mean and variance (Hollander & Wolfe). The standardised statistic is Wstar = (W − E[W]) / sqrt(V[W]); the p-value follows from Φ(Wstar).

KNOWN GAPs: tied-rank correction (MATLAB applies a small tie-correction to V[W] when ties are present) and exact permutation distribution for small samples are deferred — asymptotic only.

Parameters
xFirst sample.
ySecond sample.
alphaSignificance level (default 0.05).
tailDirection of the alternative.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(h, p, W, Wstar).
See also
vartest2, ranksum

◆ canoncorr()

CanoncorrResult nk::stats::canoncorr ( const Value & X,
const Value & Y,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Canonical correlation analysis ([A, B, r] = canoncorr(X, Y)).

Finds linear combinations U = X·A and V = Y·B such that corr(U(:, i), V(:, i)) = r(i) is maximised, with the standard orthogonality / unit-variance constraints on U and V.

Algorithm: centre X and Y; compute QX, QY from thin QR; SVD QX' · QY for the canonical directions; back-substitute through R_X, R_Y to recover A, B. r is the singular-value vector (clamped to [0, 1] to absorb FP drift).

Parameters
Xn × p first set of variables.
Yn × q second set of variables (rows(Y) == rows(X)).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
{A, B, r} struct.

Classify samples via LDA / QDA ([c, err, posterior, logp] = classify(sample, training, group, type)).

Fits a discriminant model on (training, group) and assigns labels to each row of sample. Empirical priors (n_k / N).

◆ dwtest()

std::tuple< Value, Value > nk::stats::dwtest ( const Value & r,
const Value & X,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Durbin-Watson test for first-order autocorrelation in regression residuals ([p, dw] = dwtest(r, X)).

H0: residuals are uncorrelated (DW = 2). Alternative: positive or negative first-order autocorrelation.

DW = Σ_{i=2..n}(r_i - r_{i-1})² / Σ_{i=1..n} r_i².

p-value uses the beta-approximation (Durbin & Watson 1971): the second-moment matches of DW under H0 are computed from the design matrix X and fit to a Beta(a, b) on [0, 4]. This is MATLAB's 'approximate' method. The exact Pan-1965 algorithm is a v1 KNOWN GAP — method = 'exact' is not supported and throws.

Parameters
rOLS residuals (length n, column).
XDesign matrix (n × k) used to fit the residuals.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(p, dw) — two-sided p-value, DW statistic.

◆ evfit() [1/2]

Value nk::stats::evfit ( const Value & x,
const Value & censoring,
const Value & freq,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Type-I EV (Gumbel-min) MLE fit with right-censoring and frequency weights ([parmhat, parmci] = evfit(x, alpha, cens, freq)).

Likelihood is the product of f(x_i) over uncensored observations and S(x_i) (survival) over right-censored observations, each raised to the frequency-weight freq_i. When both censoring and freq are empty or trivial, dispatches to the fast closed-form path; otherwise refines via 2-D Newton on (μ, σ) with FD gradient and Hessian and a backtracking line search.

Parameters
xObservations.
censoringLength-n 0/1 indicator (1 = right-censored). Pass Value::Empty to disable.
freqLength-n non-negative frequency weights. Pass Value::Empty to disable (uniform weight).
mrMemory resource.
Returns
[muhat, sigmahat] as a 1 × 2 row.

◆ evfit() [2/2]

Value nk::stats::evfit ( const Value & x,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Type-I EV (Gumbel-min) MLE fit ([muhat, sigmahat] = evfit(x)).

Concentrates the location out via μ = σ · log(Σ exp(x_i/σ) / n) and runs Newton iteration on the resulting 1-D equation Σ x_i e^{x_i/σ} / Σ e^{x_i/σ} - mean(x) - σ = 0. Initial guess from the moment relation var(x) = σ² · π²/6.

Numerical stability: exponentials shifted by max(x)/σ (the ratio U/T is invariant under that shift).

Parameters
xObservations.
mrMemory resource.
Returns
[muhat, sigmahat] as a 1 × 2 row.
See also
evpdf, evcdf

Value nk::stats::evfit_ci ( const Value & x,
double alpha = 0.05,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Wald CI for evfit (pci = evfit_ci(x, alpha)).

Returns the 2 × 2 confidence matrix [lo; hi] for [mu, sigma] from the observed Fisher information (central-FD Hessian of NLL). mu uses a linear Wald CI; sigma uses a log-scale CI (MATLAB convention).

◆ friedman()

std::tuple< Value, Value, Value > nk::stats::friedman ( const Value & x,
int reps = 1,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Friedman non-parametric two-way ANOVA by ranks ([p, Q, df] = friedman(x, reps)).

Ranks the k treatments (columns) within each of the n blocks (rows), then forms the tie-corrected chi-square statistic Q = [12/(n·k·(k+1)) · Σ Rⱼ² − 3·n·(k+1)] / C, C = 1 − Σ(t³−t)/(n·(k³−k)), with p = 1 − chi2cdf(Q, k−1).

NB: like kruskalwallis, this returns the statistic + df rather than MATLAB's display (tbl, stats); the primary p matches MATLAB exactly. Only reps == 1 is supported — reps > 1 (a replicated two-way layout) is rejected at the register, since its ranking does not match MATLAB here yet.

Parameters
xn × k data matrix (blocks × treatments).
repsReplicates per cell (only 1 is currently supported).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(p, Q, df).
See also
kruskalwallis, anova1

◆ gamfit() [1/2]

Value nk::stats::gamfit ( const Value & x,
const Value & censoring,
const Value & freq,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Gamma MLE fit with right-censoring and frequency weights ([parmhat, parmci] = gamfit(x, alpha, cens, freq)).

Likelihood is ∏ f(x_i)^(u_i · f_i) · S(x_i)^(c_i · f_i) where the survival is S(x; a, b) = 1 − gammainc(x/b, a) (upper-tail regularised incomplete gamma). When censoring and freq are both empty/trivial, falls through to the fast Newton path. Otherwise runs 2-D Newton on (a, b) with FD gradient/Hessian on the censored-weighted NLL, with backtracking line search.

◆ gamfit() [2/2]

Value nk::stats::gamfit ( const Value & x,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Gamma distribution MLE fit ([ahat, bhat] = gamfit(x)).

Solves the MLE system for Gamma(a, b) on positive data. The shape a is found by Newton iteration on log a - ψ(a) = s where s = log(mean(x)) - mean(log(x)) (Minka 2002 initial guess + digamma/trigamma Newton); the scale b = mean(x) / a.

Returns a 2-element vector [ahat, bhat]. KNOWN GAP: confidence intervals (bci second output) deferred — MATLAB ships them but the v1 nk form is single-output.

Parameters
xPositive sample data (1-D vector or matrix; flattened).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
[ahat, bhat] as a 1 × 2 row.

◆ gevfit()

Value nk::stats::gevfit ( const Value & x,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

GEV MLE fit ([parmhat, parmci] = gevfit(x, alpha)).

Maximum likelihood estimation of the 3-parameter GEV (k, σ, μ):

  • Initial guess from probability-weighted moments (Hosking, Wallis & Wood 1985): k_pwm = 7.8590·c + 2.9554·c² where c = 2β_1/(β_2 - β_0) − ln 2 / ln 3, σ_pwm = k·(β_0 − 2β_1) / (Γ(1+k)·(1 − 2^{-k})), μ_pwm = β_0 + σ_pwm·(1 − Γ(1+k))/k.
  • 3-D Newton refinement on (k, σ, μ) with FD gradient/Hessian on the log-likelihood, backtracking line search with support-constraint guard (1 + k(x−μ)/σ > 0 for all x).

At k = 0 the support constraint collapses to the Gumbel-max limit; the iteration handles it by treating |k| < 1e−10 via the small-k Taylor expansion of log(1+kz)/k ≈ z − k z²/2.

Parameters
xObservations.
mrMemory resource.
Returns
[khat, sigmahat, muhat] as a 1 × 3 row.
See also
gevpdf, gevlike

◆ gevpdf()

Value nk::stats::gevpdf ( const Value & x,
double k,
double sigma,
double mu,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

GEV pdf (y = gevpdf(x, k, sigma, mu)).

Three sub-families depending on the shape k:

  • k > 0 → Fréchet (heavy-tailed, lower bound mu - sigma/k)
  • k = 0 → Gumbel-for-maxima limit: f = (1/σ) e^{-z} e^{-e^{-z}}, z = (x-mu)/sigma
  • k < 0 → Reverse Weibull (bounded above at mu - sigma/k)

For k ≠ 0, the standardised t = 1 + k·(x-mu)/sigma must be > 0.

Parameters
xEvaluation points (any shape).
kShape parameter (any real).
sigmaScale parameter (sigma > 0).
muLocation parameter.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
Array of pdf values, same shape as x.
See also
gevcdf, gevinv, gevrnd, gevstat

◆ glmfit()

GlmfitResult nk::stats::glmfit ( const Value & X,
const Value & y,
GlmDistribution distr,
GlmLink link = GlmLink::Identity,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Fit a generalised linear model ([b, dev] = glmfit(X, y, distr [, link])).

Solves μ = g^{-1}(X · β) via iteratively-reweighted least squares (IRLS) with the natural / canonical link by default.

Supported distributions and canonical links:

  • 'normal' → identity
  • 'binomial' → logit
  • 'poisson' → log
  • 'gamma' → reciprocal

A column of ones is prepended automatically to X for the intercept term (MATLAB convention). Pass [] for link to use the canonical link.

KNOWN GAPs (v1):

  • y for 'binomial' must be a proportion (y ∈ [0, 1]); the [successes, trials] two-column form is not yet supported.
  • Returned stats reduced to dev (deviance) only — no standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, residuals struct.
  • 'constant' name-value pair (off/on) not supported — intercept is always added.
Parameters
XDesign matrix (n × p, no intercept column).
yResponse (n × 1).
distrDistribution family.
linkLink function (default = canonical for distr).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
{b, dev} — coefficients with intercept first, and total deviance.

◆ gpfit()

Value nk::stats::gpfit ( const Value & x,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Generalised Pareto MLE fit ([khat, sigmahat] = gpfit(x)).

Maximum likelihood estimation in two stages:

  1. Initial guess via the probability-weighted-moments estimator (Hosking & Wallis 1987, α-form): α_0 = mean(x), α_1 = mean((1 − F̂_i) · x_(i)), F̂_i = (i − 0.35)/n, k̂_0 = 2 − α_0/(α_0 − 2α_1), σ̂_0 = 2·α_0·α_1/(α_0 − 2α_1).
  2. Newton-Raphson refinement on the 2-D log-likelihood with analytical gradient and central-FD Hessian on the gradient. Backtracking line search rejects infeasible (support-violating or NLL-worsening) steps. Converges to MATLAB's Grimshaw MLE (1993) to ~1e-9 in typical samples.

Threshold θ is assumed 0 (MATLAB convention for gpfit).

Parameters
xObservations (must be ≥ 0; threshold θ = 0).
mrMemory resource.
Returns
[khat, sigmahat] as a 1 × 2 row.
See also
gppdf, gplike

std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Grouping variable → index vector ([G, GN, GL] = grp2idx(s)).

Converts a grouping variable s into a 1-based group-index column plus the group names. Ordering rules (MATLAB R2025b):

  • Numeric/logical s: groups are the sorted-ascending unique values; each name is the value formatted like MATLAB (num2str-ish). NaN maps to a NaN index and is excluded from the group set.
  • cellstr / multi-element string s: unique strings in first-appearance order; the name is the string itself.
  • A single char row / string scalar is one group label. (Categorical input and column-aligned char matrices are not yet handled.)
Parameters

mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
Grp2idxResult { G, GN, GL } (GL == GN here).

Errorif s is empty (no argument).

Draws one p × p positive-definite matrix from the inverse Wishart W ~ IW_p(Tau, df). Implementation: sample Y ~ W_p(inv(Tau), df) via Bartlett, then return inv(Y).

◆ iwishrnd_factor()

const Value & Tau,
double df,
const Value & DI,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Inverse-Wishart sample with pre-computed Cholesky factor (W = iwishrnd(Tau, df, DI)).

DI = chol(inv(Tau), 'lower'): a lower-triangular factor with DI · DI' = inv(Tau). When provided, skips the inverse-Cholesky computation. (Note: MATLAB's iwishrnd returns a different but numerically equivalent factor inv(chol(Tau, 'upper'))', which satisfies DI' · DI = inv(Tau) instead. Both produce statistically identical Inv-Wishart draws; the numerical orientation differs.)

Returns
{W, DI} — Inv-Wishart draw and the lower-Cholesky of inv(Tau).

◆ lasso()

LassoResult nk::stats::lasso ( const Value & X,
const Value & y,
const Value & lambdas,
double alpha = 1.0,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

LASSO / elastic-net linear regression ([B, FitInfo] = lasso(X, y, lambdas, alpha)).

Solves min_β,β0 (1/2n) · ||y - β0 - X·β||²

  • λ · [ α · ||β||₁ + (1 - α)/2 · ||β||₂² ] via cyclic coordinate descent with soft-thresholding. The predictors are standardised internally; coefficients are returned in the original units. The intercept β0 is the response mean minus the standardised-coefficient projection (auto-fit, MATLAB convention).

lambdas must be a vector of λ values (each ≥ 0). For an auto λ-path use linspace(0, lambda_max(X, y), 100) at the call site.

alpha ∈ [0, 1] mixes L1 (α = 1, pure lasso, default) and L2 (α = 0, ridge) penalties.

KNOWN GAPs (v1): no auto λ-path, no cross-validation, no 'CV'/'NumLambda'/'LambdaRatio' name-value pairs, no observation weights. Intercept is always included.

Parameters
XDesign matrix (n × p).
yResponse (n × 1).
lambdasLength-nLambda vector of regularisation values.
alphaElastic-net mixing parameter.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
{B, Intercept, Lambda}.

◆ lhsdesign()

Value nk::stats::lhsdesign ( ::nk::ops::RngContext & rng,
std::size_t n,
std::size_t p,
bool smooth,
LhsCriterion criterion,
std::size_t iterations,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Latin Hypercube design (X = lhsdesign(n, p[, options])).

Generates an n × p matrix where each column is a Latin hypercube sample: the unit interval (0, 1) is partitioned into n equal bins and exactly one sample lands in each bin.

With smooth = true (default) the value within each bin is (π[i] − U)/n with U ~ Uniform(0, 1); with smooth = false midpoints (π[i] − 0.5)/n are used.

criterion controls optimization over iterations trials:

  • None – single random design (fastest).
  • Maximin – pick the trial maximising min pairwise Euclidean distance between rows (DEFAULT, matches MATLAB).
  • Correlation – pick the trial minimising max absolute off-diagonal Pearson correlation between columns.

Uses the shared MT19937 stream — rng(seed) makes designs reproducible. iterations default is 5 (MATLAB convention).

Parameters
nNumber of samples (rows).
pNumber of variables (columns).
smoothtrue for (π[i] - U)/n, false for midpoints.
criterionOptimization objective (see enum).
iterationsMaximum trials for the criterion search (≥ 1).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
n × p design matrix with entries in (0, 1).
See also
lhsnorm

Latin Hypercube sample mapped to a Gaussian (Y = lhsnorm(mu, Sigma, n)).

Apply norminv to a lhsdesign(n, length(mu)) uniform design, then transform via the Cholesky factor of Sigma: Y = Z · chol(Sigma) + mu, where Z is the matrix of standard normal LHS draws.

mu must be a length-d row or column vector; Sigma must be d × d symmetric positive-definite.

◆ lillietest()

std::tuple< Value, Value, Value, Value > nk::stats::lillietest ( const Value & x,
double alpha = 0.05,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Lilliefors normality test ([h, p, kstat, critval] = lillietest(x, alpha)).

Tests the composite hypothesis that x comes from a normal distribution with unknown mean and variance. Computes the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic against the fitted normal, applies the Stephens (1974) modified statistic D* = D·(sqrt(n) - 0.01 + 0.85/sqrt(n)), and reads p / the critical value from the Lilliefors table (interpolated; p clamped to [1e-10, 0.5]).

Parameters
xSample (numel >= 4).
alphaSignificance level in (0, 1) (default 0.05).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(h, p, kstat, critval) — reject flag, approximate p-value, KS statistic D, and critical D at alpha.
Exceptions
Errorif numel(x) < 4, alpha is not in (0, 1), or the sample has zero variance.

◆ multcompare()

Value nk::stats::multcompare ( const Value & stats,
double alpha = 0.05,
McCorrection ctype = McCorrection::Bonferroni,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Pairwise post-hoc comparisons after one-way ANOVA (c = multcompare(stats [, alpha [, ctype]])).

stats is the 3rd output of anova1 (a struct with fields gnames, means, n, s, df). For each pair (i, j) of groups, returns a row

[ i, j, lower_CI, mean_diff, upper_CI, p_value ]

where mean_diff = means(i) - means(j), p_value is the two-sided t-test p adjusted for multiplicity, and CI half-width is t_crit · s · sqrt(1/n_i + 1/n_j).

Supported ctype:

  • McCorrection::Bonferroni (default in v1) — multiply each unadjusted p by the number of pairs K = k(k-1)/2, clip to 1.
  • McCorrection::LSD — Fisher's least-significant-difference; no multiplicity correction (raw t-test).

KNOWN GAP: Tukey HSD (MATLAB default) requires the studentized range distribution — not in v1.

Parameters
statsStruct from anova1.
alphaSignificance level (default 0.05).
ctypeCorrection method.
mrMemory resource.
Returns
K × 6 matrix of pairwise comparisons.

◆ mvncdf()

Value nk::stats::mvncdf ( const Value & X,
const Value & mu,
const Value & Sigma,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Multivariate normal CDF (p = mvncdf(X, mu, Sigma)).

Returns the probability P(Y ≤ X) for Y ~ N(mu, Sigma), row-wise (each row of X is one evaluation point).

Algorithm by dimension:

  • d = 1 → direct normcdf.
  • d = 2 → Owen's tetrachoric / Drezner-Wesolowsky numerical integration (16-point Gauss-Legendre).
  • d ≥ 3 → Monte Carlo with antithetic sampling (10000 draws by default). KNOWN GAP: Genz separation-of-variables quasi-MC is more accurate but not yet in v1.

Mu may be omitted (defaults to zero vector). Sigma defaults to identity. The standard-normal one-arg form mvncdf(X) is the most common usage in practice.

Parameters
Xn × d evaluation points (each row one query).
mu1 × d mean (may be empty → zero).
Sigmad × d covariance (may be empty → identity).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
n × 1 column of cumulative probabilities.

◆ mvnpdf()

Value nk::stats::mvnpdf ( const Value & X,
const Value & mu,
const Value & Sigma,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Multivariate normal pdf (y = mvnpdf(X, mu, Sigma)).

\( f(x; \mu, \Sigma) = \dfrac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}\,|\Sigma|^{1/2}}\, e^{-\tfrac{1}{2}(x-\mu)^\top \Sigma^{-1} (x-\mu)} \).

Parameters
XN × d (one point per row) or 1 × d single point.
mu1 × d mean. Pass empty Value for zeros.
Sigmad × d covariance (PSD). Pass empty Value for identity.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
N × 1 column of densities.
See also
mvtpdf, mnpdf

◆ mvnrnd()

Value nk::stats::mvnrnd ( ::nk::ops::RngContext & rng,
const Value & mu,
const Value & Sigma,
std::size_t n = 0,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Multivariate normal random samples (R = mvnrnd(mu, Sigma [, n])).

Draws n independent samples from N(mu, Sigma) via Cholesky: R = mu + Z · L' where L = chol(Sigma, 'lower') and Z is a standard-normal n × d matrix.

Supports three calling conventions for mu:

  • 1 × d row vector — same mu for every sample
  • d × 1 column vector — same mu for every sample
  • n × d matrix — per-sample location (n must match)

Sigma must be d × d, symmetric positive-definite. Non-PD inputs throw m:mvnrnd:notPD at the Cholesky step. Sigma-as-diagonal-vector shorthand (mvnrnd(mu, sigmaVec, n)) is a v1 KNOWN GAP.

Uses the shared MT19937 stream so rng(seed) makes draws reproducible.

Parameters
muLocation parameter (1×d, d×1, or n×d).
SigmaCovariance matrix (d×d, symmetric PD).
nSample count. 0 → infer from mu (1 if mu is a vector, rows(mu) if mu is a matrix).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
n × d matrix of samples.
Exceptions
Erroron shape mismatch or non-PD Sigma.

◆ nctcdf()

Value nk::stats::nctcdf ( const Value & x,
double nu,
double delta,
bool upper = false,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Noncentral Student's t cdf (p = nctcdf(x, nu, delta)).

Owen series (1965, Lenth 1989): F(x; ν, δ) = Φ(-δ) + ½·Σ_k P_k · I_y(k+½, ν/2)

  • (δ/(2√(2π)))·Σ_k Q_k · I_y(k+1, ν/2) where y = x²/(x²+ν), P_k = e^{-δ²/2}(δ²/2)^k/k!, Q_k = e^{-δ²/2}(δ²/2)^k / Γ(k+3/2), and the symmetry F(x; ν, δ) = 1 - F(-x; ν, -δ) handles negative x.

The optional 'upper' flag returns 1 - F.

Parameters
xEvaluation points (any shape).
nuDegrees of freedom (nu > 0).
deltaNoncentrality parameter.
upperIf true, return upper-tail 1 - F (default false).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
Array of cdf values in [0, 1].
See also
nctpdf, nctinv

Noncentral Student's t pdf (y = nctpdf(x, nu, delta)).

Distribution of T = (Z + δ)/sqrt(V/ν) where Z ~ N(0,1), V ~ χ²(ν), Z ⊥ V. Reduces to tpdf(x, ν) when δ = 0.

Implementation: Owen-Lenth series in terms of the regularised incomplete beta: f(x; ν, δ) = e^{-δ²/2} Σ_k a_k(δ) · g_k(x; ν) where the sum is truncated when contributions fall below 1e-16 · running_sum.

◆ nlinfit()

NlinfitResult nk::stats::nlinfit ( const Value & X,
const Value & y,
FnHandle model,
const Value & beta0,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Nonlinear least-squares fit via Levenberg-Marquardt.

Fits y ≈ fun(beta, X) by minimising ||y - fun(beta, X)||². fun is a function handle taking (beta, X) and returning a length-n predicted vector.

Algorithm: classical LM with adaptive damping (λ scaled by 10× on rejected steps, by 0.1× on accepted steps), numerical Jacobian via central differences with relative step 1e-7 · max(|β|, 1).

KNOWN GAPs: name-value 'Weights', 'ErrorModel', 'Options' not supported. Returns MSE = SSE / (n - p).

Parameters
XPredictor data (n × k).
yResponse vector (n × 1).
funFunction handle fun(beta, X) returning predictions.
beta0Initial parameter estimate.
engineEngine pointer for callFunctionHandle (required — adapters pass ctx.engine).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
{beta, R, J, CovB, MSE}.

Normal negative-log-likelihood (nLogL = normlike(mu, sigma, x, cens, freq)).

Handles the (censoring, freq) optional args:

  • censoring[i] != 0 → element i is right-censored; contribute -log(1 - F(z_i)) = -log(0.5·erfc(z_i/√2)) instead of -log(f).
  • freq[i] (default 1) → multiplies the element's contribution. freq[i] == 0 removes the element from the sum.

Boundary handling: sigma <= 0 → NaN; any NaN in x → NaN; empty x → 0.

sigmaScale parameter (sigma > 0).
xSample data.
censRight-censoring mask (empty Value for none).
freqPer-sample weights (empty Value for ones).

Matches MATLAB's default parcorr Method (OLS): for each lag k, fits the AR(k) model y_t = c + Σ_{j=1..k} φ_j·y_{t-j} by least squares on observations t = k+1..N and returns PACF(k) = φ_k (lag-0 = 1). Confidence bounds are ±numSTD/√N. Solved via the normal equations — reproduces MATLAB's QR to full precision on well-conditioned lags (N-k ≥ k+1); deeper rank-deficient lags are numerically unstable in both engines.

Parameters
yReal 1-D series.
numLagsNumber of lags; < 0 → MATLAB default min(20, N-1).
numSTDBound width in standard errors (default 2).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
(pacf, lags, bounds) column vectors (numLags+1 entries).
See also
autocorr, crosscorr

Value nk::stats::partialcorri ( const Value & Y,

const Value & Z = {},

Partial correlation between each column of Y and each column of X, controlling for the remaining columns of X (and optionally Z).

(R = partialcorri(Y, X) / R = partialcorri(Y, X, Z))

Unlike partialcorr_of(X, Y, Z), the control set varies per X column: for column j, the controls are X(:, ~j) (all other X columns), unioned with Z if supplied. Both the y and x_j columns are residualised on the control set, then the residuals are Pearson-correlated.

◆ silhouette()

Value nk::stats::silhouette ( const Value & X,
const Value & clust,
const std::string & metric = "sqeuclidean",
double p = 2.0,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Per-point silhouette coefficient (s = silhouette(X, clust, metric, p)).

For each point i with label k, computes:

  • a(i) = mean distance to other points with label k (0 if singleton)
  • b(i) = min over labels k' ≠ k of the mean distance from i to cluster k'
  • s(i) = (b(i) - a(i)) / max(a(i), b(i))

Singleton clusters are assigned s(i) = 0.

Parameters
XN × d data matrix (one observation per row).
clustN × 1 integer cluster labels.
metricDistance metric — see pdist (default "sqeuclidean").
pMinkowski exponent (used only for metric == "minkowski", default 2).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
Column vector of silhouette coefficients in [-1, 1].
See also
pdist, kmeans

◆ wblfit() [1/2]

Value nk::stats::wblfit ( const Value & x,
const Value & censoring,
const Value & freq,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Weibull MLE fit with right-censoring and frequency weights ([parmhat, parmci] = wblfit(x, alpha, cens, freq)).

Likelihood is ∏ f(x_i)^(u_i · f_i) · S(x_i)^(c_i · f_i) where S(x; a, b) = exp(-(x/a)^b) is the Weibull survival. Closed-form fast path used when both censoring and freq are empty/trivial; otherwise profiles a(b) = (Σ f_i x_i^b / Σ f_i u_i)^{1/b} and 1-D Newtons on b.

◆ wblfit() [2/2]

Value nk::stats::wblfit ( const Value & x,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Weibull MLE fit ([ahat, bhat] = wblfit(x)).

Solves the MLE system for Weibull(a, b) (a = scale, b = shape). The shape b satisfies the implicit equation

1/b + mean(log x) - Σ x_i^b · log(x_i) / Σ x_i^b = 0

solved via Newton iteration on b starting from the moment-based initial guess. Scale follows as a = (Σ x_i^b / n)^{1/b}.

Parameters
xPositive sample data.
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
[ahat, bhat] as a 1 × 2 row (scale, shape).

Weibull pdf (y = wblpdf(x, a, b)).

\( f(x; a, b) = (b/a)\,(x/a)^{b-1}\,e^{-(x/a)^b} \) for x >= 0. Convention: a = scale, b = shape. Note: std::weibull_distribution uses the opposite order (shape, scale).

◆ wishrnd()

Value nk::stats::wishrnd ( ::nk::ops::RngContext & rng,
const Value & Sigma,
double df,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Wishart random matrix (W = wishrnd(Sigma, df)).

Draws one p × p positive-definite matrix from the Wishart distribution W_p(Sigma, df) via Bartlett decomposition:

  • Factor Sigma = L · L' (lower Cholesky).
  • Sample B lower triangular with B(i,i) = sqrt(χ²(df - i)) and B(i,j) ~ N(0,1) for i > j.
  • Then M = L · B and W = M · M'.

df must satisfy df > p - 1.

KNOWN GAPs: third-argument D (pre-computed Cholesky) and the two-output [W, D] = wishrnd(...) form are deferred.

Parameters
Sigmap × p symmetric positive-definite scale matrix.
dfDegrees of freedom (> p - 1).
mrMemory resource (nullptr → process default).
Returns
Single p × p Wishart draw.
See also
iwishrnd, mvnrnd

const Value & D,
std::pmr::memory_resource * mr = nullptr )

Wishart sample with pre-computed Cholesky factor (W = wishrnd(Sigma, df, D)).

If D is empty, internally compute D = chol(Sigma, 'upper'); otherwise reuse the supplied factor (which must satisfy D' * D == Sigma). The 2-output form returns the Cholesky factor.

Parameters

dfDegrees of freedom (df > p - 1).
DPre-computed chol(Sigma, 'upper'), or Value::Empty.

{W, D} — Wishart draw and the upper-Cholesky factor.
